newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen holding firm against yen in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen holding firm against yen in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to hold firm against the yen and the mark during Asian trading time on Friday, after ending New York trade above 116 yen on Thursday, dealers said.

A growing perception that the dollar's recent sharp drop has stopped, at least for now, may encourage traders to buy dollars for yen, while the market watches for any comments by monetary officials, they added.
A trust bank dealer said short-covering and bids from Japanese investors may emerge below 115.50 yen, supporting the dollar.
"Recent comments by Japanese monetary officials have suggested that they are also concerned about the yen's rapid and excessive rise," a city bank dealer said.
He added that Japanese institutional investors may start buying dollars, as they think the risk of a further dollar fall has ended for now, given such official comments.

Dealers said they will keep focusing on comments from monetary authorities as the market seeks near-term direction. The dollar received a boost on Thursday after Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka supported the current policy of the Bank of Japan to maintain low interest rates.
His comments helped ease expectations of an imminent rise in the Japanese official discount rate by the central bank, dealers said.
Offers from overseas operators and interbank dealers are expected above 116.50 yen, weighing on the dollar, the trust bank dealer said.
"Selling by U.S. funds may put downward pressure on the dollar," the city bank dealer said.
He added that he would also watch moves by trust banks and life insurers to see whether they engage in hedge sales.
